title: Overhaul request prioritization and KV-slot garbage collection in serving scheduler
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Over the past year we accumulated several scheduling heuristics and ad-hoc KV cache behaviors to hit low-latency SLOs under realistic load. That incremental approach created variability: cache fragmentation (dead KV slots), suboptimal batch composition for mixed-length sequences, and complex preemption paths that make the scheduler hard to reason about and brittle under bursty traffic. Several recent incidents (see links) traced to stale KV entries causing cache churn and to the scheduler entering pathological enqueue loops under high small-request ratios.

Goal: Refactor the serving scheduler and KV cache lifecycle so the runtime has a simple, testable request prioritization model and deterministic KV-slot reclamation. Deliver measurable tail-latency reductions and lower per-token GPU time under mixed workloads while keeping feature parity.

Scope / What we'll change:
- Replace rule-based preemption with a capacity-aware, explicit queue system: high-priority fast-path, multi-tenant fairness queue, and opportunistic batch builder. This removes the current ad-hoc preemption code and centralizes enqueue/ dequeue behavior.
- Implement KV-slot hot-slotting and periodic compaction: mark frequently-used KV slots as hot; cold slots become eligible for fast GC during low-util windows. Make eviction deterministic (age + usage score) to avoid oscillation.
- Decouple the batching driver thread from request admission logic to allow backpressure signals (container-level token buckets) to be honored without blocking the batcher.
- Add deterministic unit and integration tests for: batch formation under mixed sequence length, KV-slot reclamation schedule, and preemption fallback behaviors.
- Small dependency bumps required for compatibility and perf tests: PyTorch -> 2.2.1, absl -> 1.6.0 (test-only upgrade), and update internal benchmark harness to use the new CUDA 12.2 test images.

Acceptance criteria:
1) End-to-end 95th percentile generation latency improves by at least 20% for mixed small/medium sequence workloads on our benchmark cluster (compare baseline dashboard).
2) KV cache eviction rate stabilizes (variance drops) and mean active KV slots per model decreases by >=10% in steady-state.
3) No regression in throughput for long-sequence streaming (>1024 tokens).
4) All new scheduler and kvcache paths are covered by unit tests; integration test that simulates bursty traffic passes in CI.
5) Migration plan validated: runtime can fall back to old behavior via a runtime flag for 2 weeks post-rollout.

Rollout plan:
- Feature branch + perf microbenchmarks (internal harness) -> PR -> canary on staging partial fleet -> compare metrics in perf dashboard -> staged rollout to 10% of serving nodes -> 50% -> full. Each step gated by automated benchmarks and on-call signoff.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: dependency upgrade (PyTorch/CUDA) exposes kernel regressions. Mitigation: keep upgrade in test images used only by benchmark fleets; do not flip production images until green.
- Risk: deterministic eviction may evict useful cold prefixes for long-lived conversations. Mitigation: hot-slot tagging window tuned conservatively; allow per-customer pinning.
